blindSummary: The killing of the territory's most publicly visible trans person, followed by a refusal to investigate. On 8 August 2024 a 33-year-old transgender woman with a large TikTok following was found beaten and bruised beside an expressway in the capital hours after posting a routine video, having previously expressed fear for her life; a human-rights group has since sued the federal government and the police for failing to investigate, seeking a court order compelling investigation and prosecution after multiple petitions were ignored — evidence that the killing is state-implicated rather than an isolated incident. Reporting on the capital's queer scene documents threats and raids alongside informal community organising. The national framework applies here unchanged: same-sex conduct criminalised with up to 14 years' imprisonment, with dating-app luring gangs a nationwide pattern; a foreign government's foreign office warned LGBT travellers in August 2026 of arrest, violence, attacks and blackmail risks.
blindSourceSummaries: A public broadcaster report (9 August 2024): a transgender TikToker known for local area-vlog content found dead — the beaten and bruised body of the 33-year-old transgender woman was found along a highway in the capital; she had expressed fears for her life the previous year; police are investigating.

A queer-culture magazine feature: reporting on the capital's queer scene alongside the high-profile killing case, documenting the surrounding climate of threats and raids and informal community organising.

A national news outlet (19 August 2026): a foreign government's latest travel advice warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation — same-sex sexual activity illegal, up to 14 years' imprisonment, and death-penalty risks under religious law in states under religious law.
